Weekly calculator //Fer ........................................ Articles //Antto What is CO2 and how does it affect us? //Antto CO2 is a greenhouse gas that traps heat in Earth's atmosphere. 

This creates the so-called greenhouse effect, which is essential to maintain the right conditions for life on our planet. However, human activities, such as burning fossil fuels and deforestation, have increased CO2 levels in the atmosphere at an alarming rate. 

This excessive increase in CO2 is causing global warming and drastic changes in our climate.

Carbon dioxide concentration in the atmosphere currently exceeds 420 parts per million (ppm). Over the last 800,000 years, CO2 concentration in the atmosphere fluctuated between 170 and 330 parts per million (levels very acceptable for the planet's sustainability), but over the last 170 years, and enormously accelerated over the last three decades, CO2 emissions have skyrocketed to values that currently reach 420 parts per million.

It is a gas that contributes to warming the planet even though it is not the only one. Other natural gases (methane, nitrous oxide) or artificial ones (fluorinated gases) are also part of the well-known greenhouse gases (GHG). In fact, their increase in the atmosphere is what triggers climate change, the climate crisis, or the climate emergency. These are three very close terms used to describe the global warming that Earth is suffering.

Official statistics confirm that CO2 emissions over recent years (except for the lockdown months and the drastic drop in activity in many countries due to the pandemic) have not decreased.

Scientific reports warn of multiple risks and impacts. For example, water supply problems, crop collapse, drinking water scarcity (for the first time in history, water is traded on the futures market, just like gold or wheat), sea level rise, species extinction, the disappearance of entire ecosystems (especially the most fragile ones like coral reefs), an increase in droughts, hurricanes, or typhoons, mass migrations for climatic and geopolitical reasons associated with them. The fragility of ecosystems grows, and many future problems are not even predictable today.

The consequences in the not-too-distant future could be enormous, and many places with catastrophic outcomes are already here.

To reduce our environmental impact, it is important to adopt energy-efficient practices. A simple way to do this is by turning off appliances when we are not using them. Many devices keep consuming energy even in standby mode, so it is important to unplug them completely. We can also use LED bulbs instead of traditional ones, since they are more efficient in energy consumption and last longer.

In addition, making sure our homes and workplaces are well insulated can help reduce heat or cold leaks, and using curtains or blinds to regulate indoor temperature. This involves sealing windows and doors to prevent heat or cold leaks.

It is important to use energy-efficient appliances and office equipment. This refers to those that have a high energy efficiency rating and use less energy to perform the same tasks as less efficient models. When choosing new appliances or equipment, it is important to look for the energy efficiency label and opt for the most efficient models available.
